paper_title: On the Role of Model Prior in Real-World Inductive Reasoning
caption: Human pairwise comparison results on three datasets, showing preferences for hypotheses with, without demos, and cases where it was hard to tell the difference.
model_annotation: The image displays three pie charts, each representing human pairwise comparison results across three different datasets: "Truthful Review," "Funny Reddit," and "Unhealthy Comments." Each chart is divided into three segments corresponding to preferences for hypotheses with demonstrations ("W/ Demos," shown in teal), without demonstrations ("W/o Demos," shown in gray), and cases where it was hard to tell the difference ("Hard to Tell," shown in blue). The legend at the top clarifies the color coding. In the "Truthful Review" chart, the largest segment is "W/o Demos" at 43.0%, followed by "W/ Demos" at 34.1%, and "Hard to Tell" at 22.9%. In the "Funny Reddit" chart, "W/o Demos" is again the largest segment at 41.5%, followed by "W/ Demos" at 37.1%, and "Hard to Tell" at 21.5%. In the "Unhealthy Comments" chart, "W/o Demos" accounts for 37.8%, "W/ Demos" for 34.8%, and "Hard to Tell" for 27.4%. All charts include percentage labels within each segment, and the segments are arranged in a clockwise order starting from the top, with the largest segment typically positioned at the top or top-right. The visual layout suggests a comparison of how often humans preferred models with or without demonstrations across different content types, with "W/o Demos" generally being the most preferred category in all three datasets.
